goal: Make the smallest evidence-backed reviewer-prompt correction so independent Cursor review judges the current diff, scope, governance, and supplied deterministic evidence without deadlocking on controller/human gates that intentionally occur later (full Assurance, final release diff-check, human approval, commit/PR verification), while preserving those later gates as mandatory and preserving Cursor's authority to flag any diff that weakens or removes them.
acceptance_conditions: reviewer prompt explicitly distinguishes current-review evidence from later controller/human gates
reviewer is told not to return CHANGES_REQUIRED solely because later-gate evidence is not yet present in the review packet
later gates including full Assurance, final release diff-check, human approval, and release verification remain mandatory and Cursor SAFE is explicitly not a substitute for them
reviewer retains authority to flag any diff that weakens, removes, bypasses, or misorders those later gates
reviewer still independently evaluates actual diff, allowed/forbidden scope, governance, fabricated/unsupported claims, weakened tests, and altered Golden expectations
no reviewer adapter, provider transport, timeout/retry policy, controller phase transition, or schema changes are introduced
tests include a deterministic regression proving the reviewer prompt carries the stage-boundary instruction and preserves the later-gate/non-substitution language
python scripts/verify_assurance_baseline.py reports ALL PHASES PASSED
independent Cursor adversarial review returns SAFE
stop_conditions: closing the defect would require changing controller phase ordering or allowing Assurance/human gates to be skipped
closing the defect would require weakening Cursor independence or read-only authority
closing the defect would require changing reviewer adapter transport, provider parsing, retry/timeouts, schemas, governance, job logic, Candidate Truth, or resume doctrine
the correction would instruct Cursor to ignore substantive missing evidence that belongs to its current review stage
